title: What is known about 1RB0LA_0RC1RD_0LD1RE_1LA0RF_0RD0LD_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_0RC1RD_0LD1RE_1LA0RF_0RD0LD_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open; analysis only begun. Sampled when the head is in A at the left end, the tape is a list of blocks such as X(n) = A> 00 (10)^n 01 and Y(a, b) = A> 00 1010 (010)^a (10)^b 01. Two rules are clear: X(n) with n even goes to Y(n/2−1, 3n/2), and Y(a, b) with a odd goes to X(b+(3a+11)/2). Together they take X(n) with n = 0 mod 4 to X((9n+16)/4). The other cases build longer lists of blocks, which so far have always collapsed back to X or Y. The full map and the halting condition are further work.

Third pass. No halt in 1018 steps (macro simulation). The tape never has two adjacent 1s at an event, and in terms of the gaps between 1s every event is a short list of runs of gaps 1 and 2 separated by single 3s.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Two rules of the map, against the run from blank tape
claims.text: X(n), n even → Y(n/2−1, 3n/2) and Y(a, b), a odd → X(b+(3a+11)/2) (with Y(0, b) = X(b+2)). Every A-event of the blank run up to 1.4·1010 steps that is X or Y with these residues is followed by the predicted event (7 cases, e.g. X(400) → Y(199, 600) → X(904) → Y(451, 1356) → X(2038)). The other cases are lists of up to five blocks, e.g. A> 00 (10)^863 (010)^19422 00 (10)^58264 (01)^2 00 1 at step 1.36·1010.

claims.title: Six rules of the block list
claims.text: With X(n) = A> 00 (10)^n 01, Y(a,b) = A> 00 1010 (010)^a (10)^b 01, Z(a,b) = A> 00 1010 (010)^a 00 (10)^b (01)^2 00 1: X(2k) → Y(k−1, 3k); Y(2i+1, b) → X(b+3i+7); X(2k+1) → Z(k, 3k−2); Z(2i+1, b) → 00 (10)^(3i+5) 00 (10)^(b−1) (01)^5 00 1; Z(2i, 2j) → 00 (10)^(3i+4) (010)^j 00 (10)^(3j+1) (01)^2 00 1; Z(2i, 2j+1) → 00 (10)^(3i+4) (010)^j (10)^(3j+6) 01. Each checked by direct simulation for all parameters below 40 (3,060 cases).

claims.title: A relabelled mirror image among the holdouts
claims.text: Mirroring left and right and renaming the states A→B, B→C, C→D, D→A turns this table into the one of 1RB0LF_1LC0RB_0LD1LA_0RA1LE_0LA0RA_1LA--- (group G02); only the start state differs, so these rules hold there in mirror image.
claims.where: the two tables, state by state

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, whole runs of equal blocks crossed at once, exact step counts) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA/py/check_msim.py run 1RB0LA_0RC1RD_0LD1RE_1LA0RF_0RD0LD_1RD--- 1e18 (macro simulator c/msim.c there, checked against the direct simulator at 109 steps by check_msim.py check)

claims.title: No pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states
claims.text: The pushdown reduction of bb6-1RB0LF_1RC0LB/c/pds.c (one side of the tape kept exactly, the other abstracted by a DFA, reachability by post* saturation) reaches a halt for every DFA with at most 6 states, on either side: TM=1RB0LA_0RC1RD_0LD1RE_1LA0RF_0RD0LD_1RD--- ./pds 6 L and R.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The leftmost segment of the list is processed by a 3/2-type rule whose parity decides whether the next segment is merged or a new segment is pushed; the rules for a general leftmost segment (10)^x (010)^y with x ≠ 2 are still to be written down.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_1LC0RB_0LD1LA_0RA1LE_0LA0RA_1LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Not known yet. The machine keeps a list of blocks of repeated words. In the simplest case a single block of n copies of 10 is turned into one of about 9n/4 copies, two passes later. Other remainders of n build longer lists, which later collapse again. How it could halt is still to be found.

facts.text: No halt in the macro simulator (checked against the direct one at 10<sup>9</sup>).
X(n) → X((9n+16)/4) when n = 0 mod 4, through Y(n/2−1, 3n/2).
No halt, proved in Lean (first 10,000 by the kernel).

sections.heading: A Collatz-like map on a list of blocks
html: When the head is in state A at the left end, on 00 1, the tape is a list of blocks. The simplest are X(n) = 00 (10)^n 01 and Y(a, b) = 00 1010 (010)^a (10)^b 01.

Two rules are clear: X(n) with n even becomes Y(n/2−1, 3n/2), and Y(a, b) with a odd becomes X(b + (3a+11)/2). So X(n) with n divisible by 4 becomes X((9n+16)/4): a Collatz-like step. From blank tape: X(400) at step 227,603, Y(199, 600), X(904), Y(451, 1356), X(2038), Y(1018, 3057).
The other cases build longer lists. For example, step 1.36·1010 has 00 (10)^863 (010)^19422 00 (10)^58264 (01)^2 00 1. So far these have always come back to an X or Y form.

sections.heading: Six exact rules
html: Sample the run when the head is at the left end in state A and the tape starts 001. With X(n) = 00 (10)^n 01, Y(a,b) = 00 1010 (010)^a (10)^b 01 and Z(a,b) = 00 1010 (010)^a 00 (10)^b (01)^2 00 1, the next sample is:

Each rule multiplies a number by about 3/2 and its parity decides what comes next: an even count is converted in place, an odd one leaves a separator 00 and the list gets longer. Every rule was checked by direct simulation for all parameters below 40.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.063). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,389 cells (31 left of the start, 35,241 right), with a density of 1s of 0.523.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A list of (10)/(010) segments, the leftmost rewritten by 3/2-type rules whose parity decides whether the list grows; six exact rules are known (checked for all parameters below 40). Open.
family: Collatz-like map on a list of blocks (X(n) -> X((9n+16)/4) for n = 0 mod 4)
